status: Local source increment after experimental 0.13.0. Matching archive publication, production deployment and full AgentOS parity remain separate gates.
problem: Raw/canonical mode was shared by a terminal but had no process-owned recovery. A child exiting without explicitly disabling raw mode left its parent in that mode, including after a same-build checkpoint resumed in another Worker.

change.terminal: A bounded stack retains owner PID, unique acquisition token, prior Boolean discipline and applied mutation generation. Repeated top-owner acquisition preserves the restore point. Non-top release splices its restore point into the next owner. Top release restores only if no subsequent mutation superseded it.
change.admission: Foreground-group callers and terminals with no foreground group acquire a recovery lease. A background caller applies raw mode without acquiring a lease. Explicit disable releases its owned lease or selects canonical mode when it owns none.
change.lifetime: Native State retains terminal references independently of descriptor lifetime. Completion releases before done/wait publication; finish_child and Drop are idempotent fallbacks. Successful exec moves ownership; failed exec retains it; children do not inherit ownership tokens. Parked handles retain their tokens in the existing heap checkpoint.
change.limits: Existing family pipe/live-process ceilings bound retained terminals and lease frames. New mutations fail EIO on generation/token exhaustion; cleanup can still unwind at the maximum generation, after which new mutations remain rejected.

before.source: Original Rust lib.rs and pty.rs from c53d2bd, with the identical new fixtures and tests.
failures: The first child exited but the native PTY still emitted LF instead of canonical CRLF; the fixture exited 91.
After R2 checkpoint/replacement, the child exited but the parent's restored marker lacked its expected carriage return.

targetedCandidate.scope: Before adding the final background-owner case; the full check covers the final fixture.

verification.rust: 16 native WASI tests and Clippy with warnings denied passed before the full workspace check. New tests cover nested/out-of-order exit, repeated acquisition, stale tokens, re-acquisition, later unowned mutation, counter exhaustion, root completion before Drop and abandoned-handle cleanup.
verification.nativeBinding: A real WASI parent runs normal exit, closed stdin, trap, termination signal, successful exec and failed exec children, both with and without a parent raw lease. It checks bytes through the native master/slave pair. A separate background-group child changes raw mode without automatic restoration; its parent explicitly selects canonical mode.
verification.checkpoint: The child consumes hel in raw mode and acknowledges raw-ready before blocking. Parent and child handles checkpoint at the original 30-second lease. The old Worker closes before a replacement opens the same native R2 store. Appended lo-CR and EOF resume the child; it closes stdin and exits. The parent observes status zero and emits restored-CRLF. Exact byte replay and stale Queue delivery retain the result. Initial hel is echoed only if the feeder delivered it before raw acquisition; both admitted scheduling orders are checked explicitly.

fullNativeCheck.scope: Full unchanged two-worker native suite repeated after the isolated cleanup suite passed. Runtime/SDK build, TypeScript, workspace Clippy and Cargo had passed in the initial check. The initial full check itself returned exit 1; its timeout and follow-on connection failure are retained above.

firstFullNativeCheck.failure: The existing 1024-object ephemeral disposal test exceeded 15 seconds; Bun killed its dangling runtime, after which the following cleanup case encountered a closed connection. Both new raw-owner cases passed.
firstFullNativeCheck.scope: The bulk fixture executes TypeScript writeFiles/readdir and context disposal, not WASI terminal operations. No cleanup or timeout code was changed.

verification.format: bun run format:check passed with the final evidence.

limits: The restored discipline is the existing raw/canonical Boolean state, not full termios or configurable control characters.
Foreground admission does not establish controlling-terminal ownership or SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU background-access enforcement.
The checkpoint proof covers cooperative same-build heap recovery, not arbitrary crashes, cross-build heap migration or published-shell resumption.
These are local native Alchemy workerd/R2/Queue tests; production latency, memory and billing are unmeasured.
